clue.text: Movie featuring Michael Caine's depiction of terminal character

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1964 war film in which Michael Caine had his breakthrough role
second meaning: the NATO phonetic-alphabet word standing for Z, the last letter

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive of Caine but merely joins the two meanings. Terminal character means the final letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The film about the 1879 battle of Rorke's Drift shares its title with the radio code word for Z.

clue.text: Italian chemist and American doctor in turn avoid putting out papers at the beginning

indicators.note: says the shortened avoid comes first in the answer
putting the papers out of the word avoid removes them from it

parts.note: taken as written, before its papers are removed
ID, identity papers

indicators.note: the American doctor sits in the word for a turn

parts.note: a go is one's turn in a game

explanation.surface: A puzzling tale of a scientist and a US physician taking turns to dodge the press early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turn' looks like 'one after the other' but means placed inside a word for turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Avogadro was the nineteenth-century Italian scientist behind Avogadro's law and number.

clue.text: Loved travelling with Aer Lingus — ultimately they take risks

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of they

parts.note: supplies only its final letter

explanation.surface: Fans of the Irish airline find flying with it a thrill for the adventurous.
explanation.walkthrough: Aer Lingus is Ireland's national airline.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for courting danger and taking chances in how one behaves.

clue.text: Man, say, is somewhat travel-sick heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the letters read upwards
only some of the letters of travel-sick are used, a run inside it

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the hyphen is used

explanation.surface: A man confesses he is a bit queasy when travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Occasionally even Joe Swash is excited with the doorknocker?

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so this collection is rearranged
taking letters only occasionally means every other letter of even

parts.note: its second and fourth letters are taken
taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: TV presenter Joe Swash gets thrilled by someone knocking at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Swash is a British TV personality, known from EastEnders. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this religious group are known for evangelising by calling at homes door to door.

clue.text: Right for electoral system to cover vote conclusively

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the system's letters go round the vote's letter, covering it

parts.note: PR is proportional representation

indicators.note: conclusively picks the final letter of vote

parts.note: supplies only its final letter

explanation.surface: An argument that a particular voting method suits the way ballots are finally counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means correct or fitting, the same sense as right in 'the right way'.

clue.text: Suspect I can't — firstly, peeping Tom will probably like it

indicators.note: as an adjective, suspect means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: firstly takes just the opening letter of peeping

parts.note: supplies only its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone protests they cannot be a Peeping Tom, a voyeur, under suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peeping Tom' looks like one phrase, but Tom is a tomcat in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male cat, and this plant famously excites cats.

clue.text: Reveals what's essentially sung over Lily Savage's entrance

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middles of sung, over and Lily are used

parts.note: only its central letters are used
only its central letters are used
only its central letters are used

indicators.note: an entrance is the way in, so the first letter of Savage

parts.note: supplies only its first letter

explanation.surface: A singer's performance over the drag act's arrival on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Lily Savage was the drag persona of the British comedian Paul O'Grady.
explanation.definitionFit: To unveil something is to disclose it, the same as revealing it.

clue.text: Tax water supply after the Times withdraw obstruction for auditors?

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, so the remaining letters bend into a new order
withdraw tells us the newspaper's letters pull out of the words tax and water

parts.note: taken as written, before both T's are removed
T is the newspaper abbreviation for the Times; the plural Times means a T leaves each word, tax and water

explanation.surface: A complaint that the water bill rises once a newspaper pulls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun with water but is the adverb from supple. Auditors here are listeners, not accountants.
explanation.definitionFit: Wax in the ear can block hearing, so it is a blockage for anyone listening.

clue.text: Displayed antelope hearts on the counter

indicators.note: counter means running the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest, a kind of antelope
H is the card-suit abbreviation

explanation.surface: Antelope hearts set out for sale on a butcher's counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' paints a shop but means in the counter direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures are hung on a wall when they are exhibited, so hung means put on show.

clue.text: Amazing, revolutionary animated character Pingu's not for everyone

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the character's name is reversed

parts.note: Popeye the Sailor Man, the cartoon character

indicators.note: U is the film certificate meaning suitable for everyone, so it is dropped

parts.note: the animated penguin, taken as written before losing a letter

explanation.surface: A claim that the children's penguin cartoon is too radical for general viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification for universal viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eye-popping is so startling that it makes one's eyes bulge, hence astonishing.

clue.text: Group of players missing header right before six-footer arrives for corner?

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for the group is lost

parts.note: a squad is a team's group of players
an ant is an insect, and insects have six legs

explanation.surface: A footballer taking a header after a tall player arrives for a corner kick.
explanation.walkthrough: The football words header and corner are misdirection; six-footer is a six-legged creature, not a tall person.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrant is one quarter of an area, which can be a corner of it; the question mark flags the stretch.

clue.text: Educational establishment ruins it every now and then

indicators.note: only some letters at regular intervals are kept, every other one

parts.note: its second, fourth and sixth letters are taken

explanation.surface: A complaint that a school is spoilt from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Uni is the informal short form of university, a place of higher learning.

clue.text: Leaders from Leyton Orient and Northampton Town worried regarding pitch

indicators.note: worried letters are fretted over and shaken up into a new order
the leaders of words are their first letters

parts.note: each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Bosses at two English football clubs are anxious about the state of their playing surface.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient and Northampton Town are English football clubs; 'pitch' is musical, not the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal describes tone, the musical quality governed by how high or low a note sounds.

clue.text: A bully briefly seizing power will be short

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the shortened word takes hold of the power letter, which goes inside
cut short, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a brute is a cruel, bullying person

explanation.surface: A tyrant who grabs power won't last long.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt means curt or sudden, so brief in manner or duration.

clue.text: Doctor I ran to with diagnosis for disorder

indicators.note: as a verb, to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A patient runs to the GP for a diagnosis of their ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' and 'disorder' set a medical scene; doctor is the verb and disorder means chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorganisation is a state of confusion and lack of order, a synonym for disorder.

clue.text: Queue behind rugby player

parts.note: a tail is the rear or behind of something
a back is a rugby position, behind the forwards

explanation.surface: Waiting in line behind a rugby player.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailback is a line of traffic held up on a road, a vehicle queue.

clue.text: Published books about defrocked nun

indicators.note: the books go about, around, the letter from nun

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: losing her frock strips off the outside, leaving the middle of nun

parts.note: only its central letter is left

explanation.surface: Religious books about a nun who has been thrown out of her order.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that is out has been released and is available, so it has been published.

clue.text: In court hearing unprepared for commotion

parts.note: to be up before a judge is to be in court

indicators.note: heard aloud, the word for unprepared matches another word in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: raw means uncooked or unready

explanation.surface: An unready lawyer at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: In many British accents raw and roar sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a noisy disturbance, which is a commotion.

clue.text: Top referee's hiding favour

indicators.note: the words are hiding the answer inside them

parts.note: the run of letters straddling these words gives the answer

explanation.surface: A senior referee secretly shows bias to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favour' looks like a noun but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer something is to like it better, which is to favour it.

clue.text: Failing that course regularly before university

indicators.note: letters at regular intervals, every other one, are kept

parts.note: its second, fourth and sixth letters are taken
the LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A student told to take a course before university, or else drop out.
explanation.definitionFit: Or else introduces an alternative, meaning if not or otherwise.

clue.text: I ring back — not prepared to be attacked

indicators.note: back means the letters run in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
to ring someone is to dial them

indicators.note: prepared means made up or worked into shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone calls back to say they are not ready to be criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone is an idiom for assaulting them, physically or verbally.

clue.text: South American cinema maybe screening Hollywood's Easy Street virtually

indicators.note: the venue screens, hides, the shorthand inside it

parts.note: a cinema is an example of a venue
EZ is American shorthand for easy

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a lane is a narrow street

explanation.surface: A cinema showing the film 'Easy Street' to an audience in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Hollywood's flags an American form; screening plays on showing films.
explanation.definitionFit: Venezuela is a country in South America, so a Venezuelan is from that continent.

clue.text: This writer's breaking pound to get quarter

indicators.note: the setter breaks into the pound letters, splitting them

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
I'm, the setter speaking of themselves

explanation.surface: The setter splurges a pound to buy a quarter of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' is the setter's I'm, the 's being is.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher divides a carcass into quarters, each a limb with its leg.

clue.text: See 26
Picture expert following glaze with polish

parts.note: a glaze is a thin film over a surface
to buff is to polish

explanation.surface: Restoring a painting: a varnish followed by a buffing shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' means a movie, not a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is an enthusiast with specialist knowledge, and a picture is a movie.

clue.text: Withstand having been separated — it's beastly

indicators.note: once the clue word is separated into with and stand, each half is swapped for a short form or a synonym: W for with, an easel for a stand

parts.note: taken as written, then split into its two words, with and stand

explanation.surface: Someone resisting after being pulled apart from a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: Split Withstand into with and stand: W is the abbreviation for with, and an easel is a stand for a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a small carnivorous mammal, so it is an animal, a beast.

clue.text: Perhaps South Pacific island's captured by surprisingly calm US

indicators.note: the island letter is held inside the rearranged letters
the letters are arranged in a surprising, unexpected new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A Pacific island seized by a placid America, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: South Pacific is the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show, not the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: South Pacific is an example of a stage show with songs, hence 'perhaps'.
